title: He Followed Jesus in Secret.
paragraphs:
He Followed Jesus in Secret.
But the Cross Changed Everything.
There is a man in the crucifixion story that many people barely notice.

His name appears quietly in the Gospels.
He does not preach a sermon.
He does not perform miracles.
He does not lead crowds.
But in one of the most painful moments in human history, he did something that required extraordinary courage.
His name was Joseph of Arimathea.
The Bible describes him as a rich man (Matthew 27:57), a respected member of the council (Mark 15:43), and a man who was “waiting for the kingdom of God.”
But John’s Gospel reveals something even more personal about him.
Joseph was a disciple of Jesus… but secretly.
Why secretly?
Because he feared the Jewish leaders (John 19:38).
That detail alone speaks to many people today.
Some people believe in Jesus quietly.

They admire Him.
They respect His teachings.
They feel conviction when they hear His words.
But their faith stays hidden.

Hidden because of pressure.
Hidden because of reputation.
Hidden because of fear of what people might say.
Joseph knew exactly what that felt like.
He was part of the council that had power, influence, and authority in Jerusalem. To openly follow Jesus could have cost him his position, his reputation, and his place among the leaders.
So for a time, his devotion remained private.
But then came the cross.
And the cross has a way of revealing what is real inside a person.
When Jesus was healing the sick, raising the dead, and feeding thousands, being near Him carried excitement.
But when Jesus was arrested, beaten, mocked, and nailed to a cross like a criminal, standing with Him became dangerous.
The disciples scattered.
The crowds disappeared.
The religious leaders mocked Him.
And Jesus hung there, dying.
Then something remarkable happened.
The Bible says Joseph went boldly to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus (Mark 15:43).
Think about the weight of that moment.

Jesus had just been executed as a criminal against Rome.
Associating with Him now was not safe.
It was not popular.
It was not politically wise.
Yet Joseph stepped forward.
The man who had once followed in secret suddenly acted with courage.
He publicly identified himself with the crucified Christ.
Matthew tells us Joseph took the body of Jesus, wrapped it in clean linen, and laid it in his own new tomb that had been cut out of rock (Matthew 27:59–60).
This was no small act.
Tombs like that were extremely valuable.
Joseph gave Jesus the burial of honor that many criminals never received.
And in doing so, he fulfilled prophecy that the Messiah would be “with a rich man in His death” (Isaiah 53:9).
Joseph may have thought he was simply honoring Jesus.
But he was also stepping into God’s greater plan.
And his story carries a powerful lesson.
Faith cannot stay hidden forever.
At some point, what we believe in our hearts must become visible in our actions.
Joseph’s story reminds us that courage does not always appear at the beginning of someone’s journey.
Sometimes it grows quietly.
Sometimes it takes time.
Sometimes faith begins in the shadows before it stands in the light.
But when the moment comes, true devotion steps forward.
Joseph did not preach in the crowds.
He did not lead the disciples.
He did not write Scripture.
But when the moment required courage, he did not stay silent.
And because of that, he became part of one of the most sacred moments in the Gospel story.
He carried the body of the Savior.
He prepared the tomb where the resurrection story would begin.
And history remembers him as the man who honored Jesus when others were afraid.
Maybe you see yourself in Joseph.
Maybe your faith has been quiet.
Maybe you believe, but you’ve hesitated to speak.
Maybe fear of opinions, culture, family, or reputation has made you cautious about showing where you stand.
Joseph’s story reminds us of something powerful:
Delayed courage is still courage.
When the moment came, Joseph stepped forward.
And when he did, his quiet faith became visible devotion.
The cross still asks every person the same question today:
Will you only follow Jesus when it is comfortable?
Or will you stand with Him when it costs something?
Joseph of Arimathea answered that question with action.
The man who once believed in secret became the man who publicly honored the crucified King.
And sometimes the greatest acts of faith happen not when crowds are cheering…
But when the world is silent.
Scripture References
Reflection Question
If you had been there that day at the cross… would you have stepped forward like Joseph did?
Or would fear have kept you silent?
Be honest.
Then ask yourself this:
Is there any place in your life where your faith is still hiding in secret?
